assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory of two-dimensional melting is a clean, analytically controlled mechanism: dislocation unbinding gives a hexatic phase with orientational quasi-long-range order and universal exponents. It is a textbook case of a simple, general mechanism behind a messy many-body transition, with reach into soft matter, colloids, superfluid films and vortex lattices. Experiments and simulations on colloids and related systems have long tested it.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (1978) and Young (1979) are the decisive authors of the dislocation-mediated melting theory and the hexatic phase. The topological-defect idea that underlies it was already recognised in 2016 through Kosterlitz and Thouless, so the three-person prize configuration looks natural, with Kosterlitz-Thouless credited as precursor. I am unsure whether the committee would want to add an experimental colloid contributor, but none is in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Nearly five decades old, with long-standing experimental confirmation in colloidal and other 2D systems. Its interpretation is stable, though the first-order versus continuous nature of melting in specific systems stays nuanced. Recognition would be overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 prize for topological defects and phase transitions is judged to have already covered the central insight
Some real 2D systems melt through first-order transitions, so the universality claim is not perfectly uniform (from my own knowledge, not verified here)
Not verified here which experiments the committee would regard as decisive

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and stochastic thermodynamics give exact, model-independent relations for work, heat and entropy production in systems driven far from equilibrium, extending the second law to single trajectories. They are a simple, universal result that has reshaped nonequilibrium statistical physics and are used for single-molecule experiments, colloids and small engines. This is close to my own field of stochastic processes, and the identification of the essential mechanism is clear.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across several people. Evans and collaborators (with Searles and Gallavotti-Cohen, the latter not in the supplied names) came first with fluctuation relations, Jarzynski gave the equality, Crooks the detailed fluctuation theorem, and Seifert built the trajectory-level stochastic thermodynamics framework. I propose Jarzynski, Evans and Seifert as the most defensible three, but omitting Crooks is a real cost and the priority between Evans and others is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally tested in RNA/DNA pulling experiments, colloidal traps and electronic systems, and established in textbooks. Timing is reasonable, although the field is still growing.
uncertainties: Attribution is hard with four credited names and missing figures such as Gallavotti, Cohen and Searles
Experimental confirmation mostly comes from small mesoscopic systems; I regard the breadth of impact as slightly narrower than for the strongest candidates
Whether the committee sees it as a physics prize topic more than a chemistry or biophysics one

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory maps a lattice problem of strongly correlated electrons onto a self-consistent impurity problem that becomes exact in infinite dimensions. It supplied the first controlled description of the Mott transition and of correlated metals and is the standard method combined with electronic-structure calculations. It combines a clear conceptual idea with broad application and with computational practice.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt (1989) established the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar (1992) made the mapping to an impurity problem; Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell, as well as Metzner himself, are not in the supplied credit. The three supplied names form a reasonable configuration, although Metzner's role makes it imperfect, and I flag this as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years old, widely confirmed by comparison with experiments on oxides and other materials, with a stable interpretation. Timely.
uncertainties: Metzner's contribution is not among the credited names, which weakens the fairness of any three-name configuration
Quantitative accuracy for real materials depends on approximations and the impurity solver
I have not independently verified the details of the early credit history

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1984 work on infinite conformal symmetry in two-dimensional quantum field theory gave exact solutions of critical phenomena and a classification of universality classes through minimal models. It is a foundational and original piece of mathematical physics that turned conformal invariance into a powerful tool for statistical physics and string theory. Its importance for universality is clear to a statistical physicist.
assessment.attribution: The Belavin-Polyakov-Zamolodchikov paper is the well-defined source, and the three credited names correspond to its authors. This is a clean, three-person configuration, although Polyakov also appears in the holography candidate, and I treat the credit as unambiguous here.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with many applications to critical systems, quantum impurity problems and string worldsheets. Experimental tests are indirect, since they come through exact exponents in 2D critical systems, so recognition as a physics prize would rely on the theory's broad reach rather than a single decisive experiment.
uncertainties: It is mainly theoretical and mathematical, and the committee tradition of requiring experimental relevance could count against it
Fields medal-style mathematical recognition may be considered more suitable
I rely on memory for the history of the critical-exponent confirmations

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene turned moire flat bands into a tunable platform for correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it launched twistronics. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle and the experiment showed it, which is a strong theory-experiment pairing. The impact on condensed-matter physics has been large and fast.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted the flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero and colleagues (2018) observed correlated insulators and superconductivity. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald would be a natural pair with Bistritzer as the third. Other groups, such as those of Dean, Young and Yazdani, are not credited, and I flag credit as only partly resolved.
assessment.maturity: About eight years since the experiments, with broad independent confirmation across groups and materials. The origin of superconductivity in the system is not settled, so the interpretation is still in motion and recognition could be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism for superconductivity is still debated
Wide field with many contributors beyond the three credited names
Possible prematurity compared with older candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 by trapping atoms at a magic wavelength, which brings a new level of precision to time keeping and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is simple and elegant, and the resulting precision is a real quantitative breakthrough with relevance to geodesy and searches for varying constants.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept, and Ye's group brought the clocks to record precision and led much of the comparison work. Two people is a clean configuration; the contribution of earlier clock work, such as Hall and Hänsch frequency combs, is already recognised by the 2005 prize, which I take from memory.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by several laboratories, with the redefinition of the second under discussion. It is timely.
uncertainties: Ye also appears in the molecules candidate, so the committee may prefer to spread credit
I am not certain how the committee weighs metrology achievements against discoveries of new phenomena
Credit for the magic-wavelength idea might include others not in the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the principle of minimal frustration explain how disordered heteropolymers fold quickly into native states, using concepts of spin-glass theory and the random energy model. It is a clean statistical-physics mechanism for a biological problem and links the physics of disordered systems with learning-like landscapes. I value this kind of cross-disciplinary reasoning.
assessment.attribution: Bryngelson and Wolynes (1987) introduced the spin-glass analogy, and Onuchic and Wolynes developed the funnel picture. Wolynes and Onuchic are the main drivers of the later theory, while Bryngelson is an important early contributor. I propose two names but a three-person configuration would also be defensible.
assessment.maturity: Influential and supported by experiments and simulations of folding kinetics, but its status as physics rather than chemistry or biophysics is less clear, and it is partly overshadowed by structure prediction advances that do not rely on this theory.
uncertainties: The field fit for a physics prize is uncertain
The role of the landscape picture in quantitative prediction is limited compared with data-driven methods
Whether the credit should include Bryngelson

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators opened a new class of matter in which edge transport is protected by topology and time reversal symmetry. The prediction by Kane and Mele, followed by the HgTe proposal and observation, established a field with a clear mechanism and strong follow-on work in materials and spintronics.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) is central to the theory, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed HgTe and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in 2007. Mele, Hasan and Xue are not equally credited across the two related candidates, so I propose Kane and Molenkamp as a minimal but incomplete pair. Credit allocation is the main problem.
assessment.maturity: The effect has been confirmed in several materials, although practical quantized transport remains limited to low temperatures. The field has matured, and the prize recognition would be timely, but it competes with the overlapping candidate B004.
uncertainties: Credit is split across Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang, Molenkamp, Hasan and others, and not all appear here
This candidate overlaps with B004 and B039, which complicates the choice
Whether the physical impact is felt mainly in materials discovery or in applications
